headline: Majors overbought across the board with whales liquidating ETH while stablecoins sit idle and funding screams expensive.
paragraphs: The regime is unified but frayed at the extremes. All seven major assets sit above their 200-day simple moving averages, and all seven MACD signals remain above their signal lines, the kind of alignment you see when a move has legs. But Bitcoin still trades 36.8 percent below its 12-month high at 78,895, Ethereum 48.1 percent below at 2,483, and Solana 60.3 percent below at 98.24. Not one golden cross appears in the book, meaning the 50-day has not yet closed above the 200-day on any of them. You have trend affirmation without the formal breakout structure that usually precedes a sustained rally. That's the tension: price is above the line, momentum says go, but the chart setup says the move is not yet canonical.

Momentum indicators are at an extreme that should concern anyone who reads technicals for a living. Bitcoin's RSI-14 sits at 82.1, Ethereum at 79.6, Solana at 86.0, BNB at 84.3, and even the weaker hands like XRP at 80.0. In a 70-to-100 range, above 80 is overbought territory on most timeframes and most books. What makes this material is that all seven names accelerated into that zone over the last seven to thirty days: Bitcoin up 25.24 percent in the week, Ethereum up 32.03 percent, Solana up 30.39 percent, XRP up 47.91 percent. Realized volatility across the complex is elevated, with Ethereum at 70 percent annualized and XRP at 81.7 percent. MACD above signal on everything says the uptrend is still intact, but overbought RSI in a volatile regime is a yellow flag, not a reason to sell. It means the market is pricing in a lot of good news and has little room left for complacency.

The leverage desk is crowded and expensive. Bitcoin perpetual funding on OKX is 0.77 basis points per eight hours, or 8.4 percent annualized, a cost that makes sense only if you believe in further upside strongly enough to absorb that drag. Ethereum and every other major trade 1.0 basis points per eight hours, 11.0 percent annualized. When funding this high persists over multiple days, longs are paying shorts to stay exposed, a sign of crowding. Open interest is substantial: Bitcoin at 2.32 billion dollars, Ethereum at 1.47 billion, Solana at 282 million. The long-to-short ratios tell a story of retail conviction: Bitcoin is balanced at 1.0, but Ethereum is 1.2 longs per short, Solana is 1.8 to 1, XRP is 2.12 to 1, and Doge is 3.52 to 1. The smaller names have lopsided leverage bets. Liquidations over the last eleven to twenty-four hours are running 1,600 to 691 per asset, with longs getting hurt roughly three to five times harder than shorts in every name except Bitcoin. Someone's conviction is being tested.

Whale flows reveal a split vote. In the last twenty-four hours, Ethereum moved 146 million dollars off exchanges (from Binance), and Bitcoin moved 118 million off, but those moves are masking a deeper picture. Stablecoins are flowing onto exchanges: USDC 137 million to Binance, USDT 100 million to Binance. Bitcoin is also flowing onto exchanges: 96 million to OKEx. That's a contradiction. Whales are building Ethereum holdings while the stablecoin powder keg (308.6 billion dollars total, up just 0.02 percent in thirty days) sits quiet and the inflow of BTC and stablecoins suggests some traders are building dry powder or positioning for a reversal. Over the weekly window, the picture oscillates sharply: week ending August 3rd, 1.13 billion off exchanges; week ending August 10th, 544 million back on; week ending August 17th, 40 million back on; week ending August 24th, 896 million back on. Whales are accumulating selectively (Ethereum out, Bitcoin splitting), but the recent weeks show a retreat from peak conviction. The 236-million-dollar stablecoin buying power sitting in whale wallets is not deployed, a form of optionality in a market that feels stretched.

Sentiment reads as Greed at 73 on the Fear and Greed index, up sharply from 25 thirty days ago and near the top of the visible range. The market has confidence. But the tape does not fully back it. Yes, BTC and ETH ETF flows have run positive for six consecutive days at the traditional-finance level: Bitcoin took in 20.8 million on the 24th, Ethereum 13.4 million, cumulative Bitcoin flows at 53.8 billion dollars year to date. That's the institutional bid. But it is balanced against elevated leverage, overbought momentum, and whales moving coins off exchanges without fully redeploying stablecoins, a posture that is neither all-in nor all-out. Fear and Greed says the crowd is confident; the positioning data says the crowd is exposed and running thin on dry powder.

Watch for a funding collapse below 0.05 percent per eight hours: that would signal longs are no longer willing to pay for exposure and conviction is breaking. Monitor whether the long-to-short ratio on Solana and Doge compresses, as those names carry the most leverage conviction and the least diversification. Track the next ETF flow day and whether the consecutive-positive streak persists: a reversal would be the first structural cue that traditional money is uncomfortable with current valuations. Finally, observe whether Ethereum's outflow reverses and Bitcoin stops flowing onto exchanges, the first sign that whales are rotating back into accumulation rather than rebalancing. The regime is up, momentum is overbought, and money is selective. The next move belongs to whoever blinks first.
